newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Some Gulf Arabs favour postponing economic summit.
newsitem.headline: Some Gulf Arabs favour postponing economic summit.

text.p: Some Gulf Arab states favour postponing a Middle East-North Africa economic summit set for November in Qatar, official Gulf sources said on Tuesday.
"The general direction now is to ask Qatar to postpone the summit...The time is not appropriate," one said of Arab anger over Israel's building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

The sources said at least three of the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates -- were rallying for postponement and even hinted at staying away if Doha hosted the summit before resumption of stalled Middle East peace talks.
"The option of not attending is there," one source said.

Kuwait said this week it had not yet received an invitation and had yet to decide on its stand. Qatar, the current GCC head, has suggested that Israel's invitation depended on the resumption of peace talks.
Senior Syrian officials are touring Arab states in North Africa to rally support for at least a postponement following a similar mission to Gulf Arab states, including Qatar.

"The message is the same...It is not to the benefit of Arab states to hold this summit at this point in time," said a senior Arab diplomat of the effort by Syria, a key Arab ally against Iraq in the 1991 Gulf War.
It has boycotted the annual event last hosted by Egypt.

The conservative oil states of the GCC have lifted the secondary Arab economic boycott of Israel -- third-party firms which deal with the Jewish state -- but do not have diplomatic ties with Israel. Bahrain is also a GCC state.
Only Oman and Qatar have trade links with Israel but ties have cooled in recent months.
